newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH's Arnault reduces stake demand in drinks firms - paper.
newsitem.headline: LVMH's Arnault reduces stake demand in drinks firms - paper.

text.p: LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault would accept 25 percent of a company blending LVMH's wine and spirits businesses with those of British groups Guinness and Grand Metropolitan , the French newspaper La Tribune, controlled by Arnault, reported on Monday.
The report signalled increasing flexibility on the part of Arnault, whose initial demand was for 35 percent in the group he has dubbed Drinksco.
LVMH recently signalled it would be willing to take less than 35 percent and analysts estimated it would hold out for 30 percent in any negotiations with GrandMet and Guinness.

GrandMet and Guinness on Friday rejected his proposal that they create a joint 70 billion franc drinks group whose brands would range from Hennessy and Moet & Chandon, J&B, Smirnoff, Gilbey's, Tanquery, Johnnie Walker and Gordon.
The British groups said Arnault's plan would add 1.5 billion pounds in tax costs.

"LVMH maintains that its plan would create more shareholder value. Determined, if needed, to increase pressure on Guinness and GrandMet to achieve the creation of a listed wines and spirits company, the French group has let it be understood that it would accept bringing the stake it seeks to a minimum of 25 percent," La Tribune said.
It reiterated Arnault's offer, made late on Friday, to sit down with the British managers to study ways to limit the tax costs of any deal.
